title: What happened in AI — Oct 18, 2026
intro: DeepSeek shipped V4.1-Flash-1017 with MIT-licensed weights and stronger agentic coding, plus its own paid search API at $0.75 per 1,000 calls. That undercuts the $5-plus rates reported for competing retrieval APIs.
Agents are also hitting friction on the open web: The Verge reports sites closing their doors to them, while new tools aim to check agent-written code before it ships.
highlights: DeepSeek V4.1-Flash-1017 is official, with MIT-licensed weights and stronger agentic coding.
DeepSeek's search API costs $0.75 per 1,000 calls; competitors reportedly charge at least $5.
One report puts a coding task on the new model at about 20 cents.
Websites are increasingly blocking AI agents, per The Verge.
Trustbut and Sphinx add checks on agent-written code before it ships.
DeepSeek has had 10 disruptions this year and is preparing user compensation.
